scenes.title: The 4 Core Analytical Pillars: TRENDLINES, CHANNELS & THE FAN PRINCIPLE

beats.hindi_tts: Pillar one: 1. The 3-Point Validation Rule. Two reaction lows establish a tentative trendline; a decisive third reaction bounce confirms an authoritative, valid up-trendline.
beats.en_subtitle: Pillar one: 1. The 3-Point Validation Rule. Two reaction lows establish a tentative trendline; a decisive third reaction bounce confirms an authoritative, valid up-trendline.

cards.title: 1. The 3-Point Validation Rule
cards.desc: Two reaction lows establish a tentative trendline; a decisive third reaction bounce confirms an authoritative, valid up-trendline.

cards.title: 2. The 45-Degree Equilibrium Angle
cards.desc: A 45-degree trendline represents the ideal sustainable balance where price advances at a pace equal to elapsed time (Gann equilibrium).

cards.title: 3. Parallel Trend Channels
cards.desc: Drawing a parallel channel line across intervening reaction highs creates a dynamic target ceiling; failure to reach the channel line warns of trend weakness.

cards.title: 4. The Fan Principle Reversal
cards.desc: When an up-trendline breaks, prices rally to form a second and third flatter trendline; a decisive break of the third fan line signals an undeniable trend reversal.

steps: 1. Two points create a tentative trendline; it requires a decisive third test and bounce to confirm validity.
2. The longer a trendline has been in effect and the more times it has been tested, the greater its significance.
3. Steep trendlines (e.g. >60 degrees) indicate unsustainable momentum and are prone to early violations.
4. A 45-degree trendline represents the golden equilibrium where price advance matches elapsed time.
5. Channel lines create dynamic boundaries: failure to reach the channel line warns of upcoming trend exhaustion.
6. A decisive breakout above an upper channel line signals trend acceleration, requiring a steeper trendline.
7. The Fan Principle: three successively flatter trendlines must break before confirming a definitive trend reversal.
8. Upon breaking a trendline, previous support becomes future resistance on the subsequent pullback retest.
